summary: This standards-track document defines a YANG data model for managing the hardware of a single server. It lets inventory and state information about physical components be read and managed through standard network management protocols.

eli5.summary: A computer has many parts, like fans and drives. This is a standard list format for keeping track of all the parts and how they are doing.

questions: what is the yang data model for hardware management
how to inventory server hardware with yang
what is the ietf-hardware yang module
how does ietf-hardware map to entity-mib
subtitle: A standard YANG model for listing a server's physical parts, their states and their sensor readings.

tldr.problem: Network management tools need one common way to identify hardware components and read their state, instead of relying on vendor-specific data or only on the older SNMP MIBs.
tldr.mechanism: The ietf-hardware YANG module defines a flat list of components, each with a name and a class, plus optional state and sensor data. A companion iana-hardware module supplies the component class identities.
tldr.outcome: Clients can inventory hardware, read operational state and sensor values, and receive notifications when state changes, with a clear mapping to ENTITY-MIB, ENTITY-SENSOR-MIB and ENTITY-STATE-MIB.

today: The metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates RFC 8348. It is a Proposed Standard, and it builds on the datastore architecture in RFC 8342.

sections.title: Introduction and Objectives
sections.content:
RFC 8348 defines a YANG data model for managing the hardware of a single server. The model covers configuration and system state, meaning status information and counters.

It is designed for the Network Management Datastore Architecture (NMDA) of RFC 8342. For servers that do not yet support NMDA, a temporary state-only module is given in an appendix.

The stated objectives are: support common properties that identify hardware components, collect important information and states, be usable as is by new implementations, map clearly to ENTITY-MIB so both can run on the same system, and support pre-provisioning of hardware components.
sections.eli5: The goal is one tidy, shared way to describe a machine's parts, so that tools from different makers can all read it.

sections.title: The Hardware Data Model
sections.content:
The ietf-hardware module has a top-level hardware container with a read-only last-change time and a flat list called component, keyed by name. There is no nested tree of parts. Instead, a component can name a parent and a parent-rel-pos, and a read-only contains-child list shows the reverse links.

Each component has a mandatory class leaf, which is a YANG identity describing the hardware type. Other leaves identify the part: description, hardware-rev, firmware-rev, software-rev, serial-num, mfg-name, model-name, alias, asset-id, is-fru, mfg-date, uri and uuid. A physical-index leaf exists when the entity-mib feature is supported.

The iana-hardware module defines identities for the types in the IANA-maintained IANA-ENTITY-MIB registry, such as chassis, power-supply, fan, sensor, module, port, cpu, battery and storage-drive. Vendors are encouraged to use one of these directly or derive a more specific identity from one.
sections.eli5: The model is a simple list of parts, like an inventory sheet. Each part has a name, a type such as fan or drive, and facts like its serial number.

sections.title: Component State, Sensors and Notifications
sections.content:
When the hardware-state feature is supported, each component has a state container with admin-state, oper-state, usage-state, alarm-state, standby-state and state-last-changed. Only admin-state is writable. Its values are unknown, locked, shutting-down and unlocked. The operational state can be unknown, disabled, enabled or testing.

When the hardware-sensor feature is supported, a component can have read-only sensor-data with a value, value-type, value-scale, value-precision, oper-status, units-display, value-timestamp and value-update-rate. The value type says what is measured (for example celsius, rpm or watts), and the scale gives an SI prefix from yocto to yotta.

Three notifications exist: hardware-state-change, sent when /hardware/last-change changes, and hardware-state-oper-enabled and hardware-state-oper-disabled, sent when a component moves into those states.

When the server detects new hardware, it creates an operational entry. If configuration is supported and a configured entry has the same class, parent and parent-rel-pos as the detected part, the entry uses the configured values, including the name. That is how pre-provisioning works.
sections.eli5: Each part can also say whether it is switched on, working, busy or in need of help. Sensors report numbers like temperature or fan speed, and the machine can send an alert when a part switches state.

sections.title: Relationship to the Entity MIBs
sections.content:
If a device also implements the ENTITY-MIB (RFC 6933), each entry in /hardware/component maps to one EntPhysicalEntry. Writable MIB objects become config true nodes, with one exception: entPhysicalSerialNum is writable in the MIB but read-only in YANG. The physical-index leaf MUST hold the matching entPhysicalIndex.

The class leaf maps to both entPhysicalClass and entPhysicalVendorType. If the identity is, or derives from, an iana-hardware identity, entPhysicalClass takes the matching value. Otherwise it is other(1).

Components with a sensor-data container map to the ENTITY-SENSOR-MIB (RFC 3433), and components with a state container map to the ENTITY-STATE-MIB (RFC 4268). The RFC gives a table for each mapping.
sections.eli5: Older tools used a different format called a MIB. This document includes a translation chart, so each old field has a matching new one.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The modules are meant to be accessed with NETCONF or RESTCONF, whose mandatory secure transports are SSH and TLS. The NETCONF access control model (RFC 8341) can limit which users see or change which data.

Writable nodes can hurt if unprotected. Setting /hardware/component/admin-state to locked or shutting-down can disrupt services, from those on one port to those on a whole device.

Readable data can also be sensitive. The component list exposes vendor, model, version and device-identification details, sensor-data/value may expose physical sensor readings, and state can reveal which resources are active and which are on standby. Read access should be controlled too.
sections.eli5: Switching a part off can break things, and the parts list tells outsiders exactly what the machine is made of. So only trusted people should be allowed to read or change it.

sections.title: IANA Considerations
sections.content:
The iana-hardware module is IANA-maintained and is meant to mirror the IANA-ENTITY-MIB module. When a new value is added to the IANAPhysicalClass textual convention, the same class is added as an identity derived from ianahw:hardware-class. Each update adds a new revision statement in front of the existing ones.

The document registers three URIs in the IETF XML Registry and three modules in the YANG Module Names registry: iana-hardware (prefix ianahw), ietf-hardware (prefix hw) and ietf-hardware-state (prefix hw-state).
sections.eli5: A shared registry keeps the list of part types up to date, so the new format and the old one never disagree about what a fan or a battery is.

sections.title: The Appendix State Module
sections.content:
Appendix A is non-normative. It defines ietf-hardware-state, a temporary read-only copy of the model for implementations that do not yet support NMDA. In its tree diagram every node is marked deprecated and read-only.

The same three notifications appear there with status deprecated. Servers that support NMDA are expected to use ietf-hardware instead.
sections.eli5: For machines that are not ready for the new setup, there is a simpler read-only version to use for a while.
